title: Document onboarding and AI-assisted roadmap workflows

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Contributors need a clear route from reading the docs to completing an existing slice. Users need worked examples for a blank project and for an AI code review converted into a roadmap, with slicer presented as AI-friendly.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: Documentation acceptance: both example outlines import; priorities and dependencies select the expected next item; the start/done/render/check loop succeeds. Check links and current CLI flags.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Expand existing guides with tool-neutral prompts, small importable outlines, review triage, priority and queue ordering, and the contributor workflow. Correct ID configuration, started-item precedence, JSON failure reports, and atomic-write versus writer-lock descriptions.

**Not in this slice:** CLI changes, new dependencies, or implementing the example projects themselves.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Both documented outlines were extracted and exercised against local source in disposable workspace directories: dry-run, import, priorities, score sorting, stored ordering, dependencies, start/done, and check passed. All 53 local documentation links and anchors resolved; git diff --check passed.

The unit suite ran 443 tests: 439 passed, 1 optional live-legacy test skipped, and 3 failed because workspace-local temporary directories inherit this checkout's .slicer and Git roots. The failures are the two outside-project tests and the not-a-Git-repository test; a normal external temporary directory was not used under this session's workspace restrictions. No application code changed. The repository slicer check passes with 52 items.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Leave changes uncommitted for owner review.
